subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — perf targets and decision follow-up
messages:
From: James Chen <james@avarobotics.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow up on today’s call — perf targets and next steps

Neha / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can decide between Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity:  

- Primary workload: multi-turn chat for field robots (low-latency instruction + telemetry summarization).
- Target p95 generation latency: <120ms (ideally <100ms) for the 512-token context path.
- Sustained throughput: ~50 requests/sec (embeddings and short chat combined), with occasional peaks to 120rps for 5–10m.
- Data sensitivity: logs can be sent to Redwood but we prefer to keep PII out of model inputs; storing KV caches on provider side is acceptable.

Attaching our QoS report from last week (Ava_Prod_QoS_Report.pdf) for reference.

Questions:  
1) Based on these numbers, do you recommend Hosted or Dedicated?  
2) If Dedicated, what sizing do you typically recommend for predictable p95 <120ms at 50rps?
3) If Hosted is possible, what guarantees (or best-practice configs) get us close on p95?

Also looping in procurement for timeline visibility. Looking to decide within two weeks.

Best,
James Chen
Head of Platform
Ava Robotics

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: James Chen <james@avarobotics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@avarobotics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow up on today’s call — perf targets and next steps

James — thanks for the clear recap and the QoS report. High-level answers below, plus proposed next steps.

Short answer: Dedicated is the safer path for sustained 50rps with tight p95 targets. Hosted can work for many customers but requires either committed capacity or carefully tuned caching/batching to hit consistent p95s for 512-token paths.

Tradeoffs:  
- Dedicated: predictable latency/throughput, isolated GPU pools, and direct control over batching and KV cache warm-up. Recommended for steady 50rps sustained + tight p95 SLOs.
- Hosted: faster time-to-value and autoscaling for peaks, but multi-tenant variability can make consistent p95 <100–120ms harder without reserved capacity.

Sizing ballpark for Dedicated (initial pilot):  
- Start: 2 reserved inference nodes equivalent to 4x A100 per node (baseline concurrency tuned for 50rps), autoscale threshold to add 1 node at 80% utilization.  
- Optimizations: enable prefix/KV caching and model quantization profile we discussed to shave token compute.

If you’d like we can:  
1) Spin up a 2-week dedicated pilot (isolated tenant) with monitoring dashboards and token-level latency breakdowns.
2) Run a short perf sweep during the pilot with your representative traces from the QoS report to validate p95.

Next steps:  
- If you want Dedicated pilot, Marissa can draft sizing/pricing and procurement can start review (we can also provide a short trial contract + redlines).
- If you want Hosted-first, we’ll propose an autoscale + committed concurrency config and run a short validation.

Attaching internal pricing template and a sample pilot plan (see Drive link in metadata).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: James Chen <james@avarobotics.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@avarobotics.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow up on today’s call — perf targets and next steps

Looping in recommended pilot configuration and an engineering checklist so we can get you validated quickly.

Pilot recommendation (Dedicated):
- Environment: Dedicated capacity in us-west region, private tenant (no shared GPUs).
- Initial fleet: 2 nodes (each node ~4x A100 equiv), baseline autoscale +1 node at 80% sustained util.
- Runtime config: KV cache enabled, sequence length cap 512 for chat path, low-latency kernel selection, and per-route batching cap at 8 to keep tail latency low.
- Observability: Redwood Console dashboards (p50/p95/p99), tracing hooks, and token-level latency breakdowns enabled.
- Timeline: spin up within 5 business days after PO; 2-week validation run after warm-up.

Estimated committed cost (ballpark for pilot): $18k/month (pilot discount applied). If pilot validates, we’ll provide an annual reserved commitment quote with unit pricing.

Procurement — to expedite: I’ll circulate a short pilot SOW + our standard MA with redlines. James — if you want, share the preferred billing entity and a PO contact and we’ll attach the draft redlines for review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call with your infra lead to confirm traces to run.

— Marissa Cole
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
